title: atlas-search(fleet-search): HOME unset/empty resolves state/config/token paths relative to the CWD (literal ~ dir)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/design-architect
labels.description: Filed by the repo design architect job

body:
## Problem

In atlas-search (and its fleet-search port), every home-directory helper treats a missing `HOME` as the literal relative path `~`, and an empty `HOME` as the empty path — so state/config/token paths resolve **relative to the current working directory** instead of failing or resolving to the user's home.

The helper shape, copied in at least six places:

```rust
std::env::var_os("HOME").map(PathBuf::from).unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("~"))
```

- `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-search/src/server.rs:202` — `default_service_config_path()` (the `init`/`serve` service config, which contains the client bearer tokens)
- `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-search/src/fetch_model.rs:41` — `state_root()` / `model_dir()` (fetch-model provisioning + lock)
- `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-search/src/service.rs:50` — `home_dir()` (client token config `~/.config/atlas-search/client.json`)
- `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-search/src/main.rs:248` — `home_dir()` (`default_db_path()`, `resolve_model_dir()`, `resolve_ort_lib()`)
- `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/src/turso.rs:210` — `home()` (Turso token cache `~/.cache/atlas-search/turso-token.json`)
- `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-search/src/client.rs:53` — `home_dir()` (serving-host marker + the same client-token path, ported in fleet step 5)

## Verified (this run, laptop, real debug binary, probe `~/git/fleet/probe-atlas-home`)

In a scratch working directory:

- `env -u HOME atlas-search init` → exit 0, prints `wrote service config ~/.local/state/atlas-search/service.json`, and actually creates `./~/.local/state/atlas-search/service.json` under the CWD.
- `HOME= atlas-search init` → exit 0, prints `wrote service config .local/state/atlas-search/service.json`, and creates `./.local/state/atlas-search/service.json` under the CWD.

Current main `beaad887b0` contains the identical helpers at the lines above.

## Why it matters

- `init` reports success while writing the service config — which holds freshly generated client bearer tokens (0600) — into whatever directory the caller happened to be in (potentially a git checkout or shared dir), where a later `serve`/client run with a normal `HOME` will never find it. The service silently appears unconfigured.
- The same CWD-relative drift hits the model snapshot dir, the Turso token cache, and the fleet-search serving-host seat marker, so seat detection and token resolution can silently disagree with the service.
- Contrast inside this repo: `pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:999` treats a missing `HOME` as a hard error with context (`no HOME for ~/.ssh/known_hosts; pass --ssh-host-key`), and fleet-config was fixed for the empty-env half of this class in #5473. Atlas/fleet-search never got either half.

## Acceptance criteria

- An empty `HOME` is treated as unset at every site above (atlas-search, atlas-core, fleet-search).
- With `HOME` unset/empty, no atlas-search or fleet-search verb creates or reads a path under `./~` or `./.local` / `./.config` / `./.cache`: it either fails loudly naming `HOME`, or resolves the real home directory another way (e.g. passwd entry) — one consistent rule, shared where practical instead of six copies.
- Regression tests pin both shapes (unset and empty) for at least the service-config path and the fleet-search serving-host marker.
- Normal behavior is unchanged when `HOME` is set: `init` writes `~/.local/state/atlas-search/service.json`, and existing path-resolution tests stay green.
